newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle Jan-Apr sales up 18 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Nestle Jan-Apr sales up 18 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Nestle SA sales rose more than 18 percent in the first four months of 1997 from the year-earlier period, chairman Helmut Maucher said, adding he expected higher volume growth this year.
He also said he was confident Nestle would meet its profit targets for 1997 barring major unforeseen problems.
"The current year has started out well," he said to the annual shareholders meeting.

"It is clearly the effect of the foreign exchange rates that produced a sales growth of over 18 percent in the first four months of the year. But volume sales also saw a good development," he said without elaborating.
"It is naturally premature to venture a prediction for our profits. Nevertheless, we see no reason why they should not once again demonstrate a very satisfactory progression."
Maucher said it would be imprudent to extrapolate figures in the first four months of 1997 for the full year because exchange rates will be comparatively less favourable in the second half.
"Moreover, if the dollar should show any weakness, the slowdown in our growth would be even more noticeable," he said.
"I am however confident that we will close the current year with an increase in sales and profits perfectly in line with our targets, as long as no major unforeseen events occur."
Maucher said Nestle had carefully analysed the situation that led to volume growth of only 2.7 percent last year, which he called "relatively weak".
"It is a temporary problem and will not occur again," he said.
"Our position in the different markets should let us attain a higher real rate of growth in this year and in coming years," he added.
In his speech, Maucher dropped a reference to an expected volume growth of four percent this year that was found in his prepared text.
